Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit target: the single supplied existing 360-degree interior panorama. Make a careful local window-treatment addition only. Preserve the full 360x180 equirectangular projection, EXACT original camera orientation, framing, image content and 2:1 aspect ratio. Retain room geometry, all window/door openings and black frames, furniture, equipment, plants, artwork, materials, original daylight and colors. Do not redesign the room, move the camera, crop, zoom, add windows or cover doorways. Keep horizontal wrapping continuous at left/right edges and original ceiling/floor distortion; this is a spherical texture, NOT a normal perspective photo. Add physically mounted window treatments with realistic folds, thin rails, contact shadows. Keep panels mostly open to preserve daylight and plants. Update any SAME visible window seen in adjacent rooms consistently. No text/watermarks. Output one full-resolution 2:1 panorama.
Style: MUJI-inspired cream and neutral pale oak: unbleached ivory voile with oatmeal linen outer panels.
Room: LIVING. Add near-ceiling double tracks and full-length soft curtains to BOTH living exterior windows (the wide left window AND the narrow right-edge window; treat seam correctly), outer panels gathered at jambs, sheer lightly drawn over glazing. Add matching curtains to dining window visible in center background, and neat partly raised short ivory wipe-clean roller blind to distant kitchen glazing. Keep TV, sofa, plants and walkways unobstructed.
